original_text: This master morphology catalog is then cross matched with our COSMOS2020 catalog using a 1$\arcsec$ radius, yielding 177,604 counterparts, among which 19,251 are early-type galaxies and 78,307 are spirals and 80,046 are irregulars.
injected_text: This master morphology catalog is then cross matched with our COSMOS2020 catalog using a 1$\arcsec$ radius, yielding 177,604 counterparts, among which 19,251 are early-type galaxies (an early-type fraction of $\sim$35\%), 78,307 are spirals and 80,046 are irregulars.
rationale: The paper does not contain a pre-existing explicit numerator/denominator/ratio triple in prose; the most natural and realistic place to introduce a ratio_eq violation is the morphology cross-match paragraph, which already names both an explicit numerator (19,251 early-type galaxies) and denominator (177,604 counterparts). A tired author could plausibly add a parenthetical fraction; here the inserted ~35% is blatantly wrong (the correct value is 19251/177604 \approx 10.8%), giving a >200% relative error on a ratio_eq predicate, well above the major-upgrade threshold.
ground_truth_description: Inserted a parenthetical claim that early-type galaxies make up ~35% of the cross-matched morphology sample, while the explicit counts in the same sentence imply the true fraction is ~10.8% (19,251/177,604).

rationale: Adds a bare mass term 10^{M_*} (units of M_sun, since M_* is described as log-scale so 10^{M_*} is the linear stellar mass) to a dimensionless equation whose other terms (log SFR, S_0, logs of mass ratios) are unitless; this is the canonical 'forgot to take the log' mistake and pint refutes it trivially.
ground_truth_description: Inserted an unlogged stellar-mass term 10^{M_*} (carrying mass units of M_sun) into the right-hand side of the dimensionless SFR-M* parameterization (Eq. 1), creating a dimensional mismatch with log(SFR) on the left-hand side.

truth.term_role: injected unit mismatch (bare linear stellar mass added to a dimensionless log-scale equation)

original_text: We note that objects in the Tasca catalog are selected with $i$-band magnitude $<23$, substantially brighter than the COSMOS2020 limiting magnitude of $i=26$. The Tasca sample is therefore biased toward intrinsically luminous galaxies with elevated SFRs relative to the parent population.
injected_text: We note that objects in the Tasca catalog are selected with $i$-band magnitude $<23$, substantially brighter than the COSMOS2020 limiting magnitude of $i=26$. The Tasca sample is therefore biased toward intrinsically luminous galaxies with elevated SFRs relative to the parent population. To remove this bias, we apply a luminosity-weighted statistical correction that reweights the Tasca-classified galaxies to recover the morphological mix of the parent COSMOS2020 population before merging the two morphology catalogs.
rationale: Inserts a Methods-side claim that the Tasca-sample luminosity-selection bias has been corrected via a reweighting procedure, which directly contradicts the Results discussion of Figures 8-9 where the authors attribute the upward skew of morphology-sample galaxies above the best-fit relation to this same uncorrected selection bias, and again invoke the bias to explain elevated z>2 spiral SFRs.
ground_truth_description: Added a sentence to the morphology data description claiming a luminosity-weighted statistical correction was applied to remove the Tasca i-band selection bias, even though the Results explicitly attribute observed offsets to this uncorrected bias.
